keys.meaning: Product idea and audience in the user's own words.
keys.display: Tell me about your idea in your own words: what is it, and who is it for?
keys.spoken: Tell me about your idea in your own words: what is it, and who is it for?
keys.helpText: A sentence or two is plenty.

keys.meaning: A secret-bearing answer whose text must never reach speech, captions, logs, crash data, telemetry, or persisted state. Registered as the FIX-017 governed authority for final-boundary privacy tests (worktree candice/wt-tests-harness, base b54aec0).
keys.helpText: Your answer is never spoken, shown, or logged.

keys.meaning: A personal answer that is never spoken or captioned unless the user explicitly opts in. Registered as the FIX-017 governed authority for final-boundary privacy tests (worktree candice/wt-tests-harness, base b54aec0).
keys.helpText: Spoken only when you explicitly opt in.

keys.meaning: Kaizen Recipe target, purpose, and audience.
keys.display: What are we trying to make better? It can be an app, website, funnel, process, document, automation, or something else.
keys.spoken: What are we trying to make better? It can be an app, website, funnel, process, document, automation, or something else.
keys.helpText: A sentence or two is plenty. If you do not know the technical category, I will infer it and confirm.

keys.meaning: Kaizen Recipe location and available access.
keys.display: Where can I find it so I know where to work?
keys.spoken: Where can I find it so I know where to work?
keys.helpText: Current folder, GitHub repo, a URL, a hosted platform, or a local document. "I do not know" is fine — I can look at the current folder and tell you what I find.

keys.display: What would you especially like me to make better? This helps me aim, but it does not limit what I can notice.
keys.spoken: What would you especially like me to make better? This helps me aim, but it does not limit what I can notice.
keys.helpText: Examples: easier to use, fewer bugs, faster, safer, better design, better sales. Or "I'm not sure — help me decide."

keys.display: How much should I work on each time? I usually recommend about 3 to 7 useful things. Five is a good starting point.
keys.spoken: How much should I work on each time? I usually recommend about 3 to 7 useful things. Five is a good starting point.
keys.helpText: Five is the recommended default. Critical findings may displace lower-priority items, but a cycle never silently exceeds the chosen scope.

keys.display: Would you like me to only tell you what I recommend, or may I safely make and test improvements for you too?
keys.spoken: Would you like me to only tell you what I recommend, or may I safely make and test improvements for you too?
keys.helpText: Mode A inspects and reports without modifying. Mode B is the recommended default: branch, change, test, revert failures, commit to a non-production branch, stop before merge or deploy.

keys.display: How can we check that the change really helped instead of just looking different?
keys.spoken: How can we check that the change really helped instead of just looking different?
keys.helpText: You do not have to know the answer — I will recommend proof based on the target type: tests and a build for an app, a live flow check for a website, and so on.

keys.display: How often should I come back and check this again?
keys.spoken: How often should I come back and check this again?
keys.helpText: Asked last on purpose — the answer depends on what we are improving and where it lives. "I don't know" is valid; I will infer and you can correct me.

keys.display: This is your Kaizen Contract. Do you approve it?
keys.spoken: This is your Kaizen Contract. Do you approve it?
keys.helpText: Nothing runs on a schedule until you approve. If you want changes, I revise the Contract and ask again.
